svg.title: RK2 midpoint on a vortex
svg.desc: Left: per-step growth of the radius of a rotating tracer against the angular step, for four integrators; the explicit midpoint method used by Flow always grows. Right: a tracer started inside a small, busy vortex is thrown out to a radius near 2.7 at the default 0.1 second step.
svg.text: The step Flow takes against the rotation it integrates
Rotation z' = i Omega z, zeta = Omega dt. The exact map has modulus 1. Default 10 fps means dt = 0.1 s.
Growth of the radius per step
A tracer in the 6 MiB, 400% vortex
Circles are the conserved level lines of the stream function: a good integrator keeps tracers on them. Midpoint grows as zeta^4/8 per step for small zeta.
Analytic field with the 20 units per second speed cap; Flow samples a cached grid by bilinear interpolation, which changes the numbers a little.
